beliefs.practice: Create and reuse a single long-lived MongoClient (connection pool) instance read from DOCUMENTDB_URI in the environment; do not open a new client per request.

Keep database credentials out of source control: read the connection string from an environment variable and store secrets in Azure Key Vault (or similar) rather than files; never log the raw connection string.
Provision throughput (RU/s) appropriately for the sample_retail_06 database/collection and prefer autoscale or shared database-level throughput to avoid 429 throttling during bursts.
Create a compound index on the fields used for the order-history queries (for example {customer_id:1, order_date:-1}) so customer lookups and recent-order sorts are index-covered.

For vector search, create a vector index on the embedding field using the platform's vector index type (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and ensure vectors are stored with consistent dimensionality and normalization.
Use projection to return only required fields (e.g., order id, date, total) instead of whole documents to reduce RU consumption and network payloads.
When building aggregation pipelines, put $match stages before $group/$sort and ensure the $match can use an index to avoid blocking in-memory sorts.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors and throttling (HTTP 429 or MongoDB equivalent), honoring any retry-after header returned by the server.
Validate query performance by running explain() on important queries and aggregation pipelines and adjust indexes until the explain plan shows index seeks instead of collection scans.
Make seeding and migration scripts idempotent (use upsert or check-and-create) so tests and repeated runs do not duplicate data or create conflicting indexes.
Require TLS/SSL for connections (TLS=true in connection string) and validate server certificates when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster.
Implement pagination with range-based cursors (e.g., order_date/_id anchors) or the driver's cursor.batch_size rather than using skip for large offsets to avoid costly scans.
In the agent memory, normalize natural-language time references (e.g., 'last month') to explicit ISO date ranges and store them in conversation state so follow-up queries resolve deterministically.
Create covering indexes that include fields used in both query predicates and projections when you need very low-latency, index-only responses for summaries (e.g., include order_total in the index).
Monitor RU/s consumption, request charge, throttling, latency, and index usage (metrics in the portal or via monitoring APIs) to tune throughput and indexes.
Lock down network access with firewall rules, VNet/private endpoints, or IP restrictions so the cluster is not publicly accessible from arbitrary IPs during development or testing.

Keep the MongoDB driver version compatible with the server wire protocol version exposed by the Azure DocumentDB (Mongo) cluster and avoid using server features not supported by the managed Mongo API.

For vector search results, store and return lightweight metadata separately from the vector field so similarity searches only load embeddings during ANN search and fetch full document fields if needed.
Configure sensible MongoClient timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) to fail fast in bad network conditions and avoid stuck requests in the agent workflow.

Use collection-level schema validation (JSON Schema validators) where possible to enforce required fields and types for orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, total, items) rather than relying only on application checks.
Use bulk writes (bulk_write or insert_many with ordered=False) to seed many documents efficiently and to reduce round-trips and RU cost.
Avoid creating unnecessary indexes: each index increases write cost and RU usage—create only the indexes used by queries and remove unused ones after measuring usage.
Capture and log request charge (if available) and operation latency for each key query in tests so you can spot expensive operations introduced by the agent.

Run tests against a dedicated test database/collection (e.g., sample_retail_06_test) and clean up data after tests to avoid interfering with production or other test runs; control the connection string via environment variables.
Cache frequently-read static reference data (product catalog, status codes) in the application or agent memory to reduce repeated DB reads and RU charge for conversational flows.
